title: ⚡ From electric signals to functional silicon

paras: Read the signal path before the chip catalog: electricity → analog conditioning → digital logic → state → conversion → computation and I/O.
Continuous-valued voltages and currents; amplifiers, oscillators, filters and sensor conditioning. Real analog systems have noise, bandwidth and nonlinearity.
Logic levels interpreted as discrete states. Combinational circuits produce outputs from current inputs; sequential circuits hold state with latches, flip-flops and registers.
ADC turns sampled analog input into digital codes; DAC reconstructs an analog output from digital codes. Clocking, reference voltage and quantization matter.
Switching regulators, MOSFET power stages and power-distribution networks convert, control and protect electrical energy.

blocks.h2: How a sensor reading becomes a software event
paras: Physical quantity → transducer → analog amplifier/filter → ADC → MCU/SoC peripheral → interrupt or DMA → driver → application → decision → DAC/PWM/actuator.

Edge meanings: transducer converts a physical quantity into an electrical signal; analog front end conditions it; ADC quantizes it; bus/peripheral exposes a register or buffer; interrupt signals completion; DMA may transfer data without CPU copying each byte; the application applies policy.
Boundary: not every design contains every stage: digital sensors may integrate an ADC and speak I²C or SPI; a purely analog feedback circuit may use no CPU.

CPU, memory, radio, PMIC, Ethernet PHY and FPGA describe functions or implementation styles . IC, package, module, PCB and SoC describe different physical integration levels. A SoC can combine CPU cores, GPU, memory controllers and peripherals, but external DRAM, storage and power components may still be required.
